text: Source: Disclosable Restructuring Paper RES01493 for P176619 (27 March 2026; a Level 2 restructuring, approved 11 March 2026 per the June 2026 ISR). Compared with the PAD:
Objectives: no change; the PDO stays 'to improve the efficiency of water services in Jordan' (summary table p. 11; PAD p. 21).

Components: scope unchanged, but US$12 million moves from Component 2 (energy efficiency, US$54 million) to Component 1 (NRW reduction, US$209 million) because energy-efficiency procurement was slow; Component 2 keeps the energy-efficiency (US$21 million) and solar PV (US$17 million) sub-projects already contracted or tendered and defers further studies (pp. 7, 9). MWI's fiduciary role for sub-component 3.1 passes to WAJ (pp. 7, 9).

Performance-based conditions: PBC 1 reworded around the NRW digitization roadmap and SCADA coverage (unchanged at US$5,001,670); PBC 2.1 scaled up to US$24,510,185 by absorbing PBC 3 and most of PBC 2.2; PBC 2.2 and PBC 3 dropped; PBC 4 adds digital dashboards and cuts verifiable annual allocation plans from four to three; PBC 5 adds dam safety maturity matrices and rises to US$6,500,169; eligible PBC expenditures widened to fixed costs of WAJ, MWI, JVA and the water companies; the Jordan Audit Bureau verifies PBCs (pp. 7-9).

Results framework (p. 10): NRW reduction target 10,000,000 to 7,000,000 m3/year; electricity use reduced 81 to 60 GWh/year (PV capacity revised from 41 to 26 GWh/year in the final feasibility study, and some sub-projects financed by others); km of networks rehabilitated 1,800 to 1,500; DMAs 180 to 90 (of which high-refugee areas 75 to 35); renewable capacity 41 to 25 MW; GHG reduction 41,796 to 35,000 t/year; the customer-feedback indicator dropped with PBC 3. Reason: the sub-projects selected are mostly primary-line replacement, which costs more per km and does not create DMAs (pp. 9-10).

Financing: no cancellation and no new financing; total remains US$300 million (IBRD US$200 million, GCFF US$50 million, AFD US$50 million); disbursement estimates are revised (US$17 million in FY26, US$135 million in FY27, US$100 million in FY28, US$46 million in FY29) (pp. 6, 11).
Closing date: no extension; it stays 31 December 2028 (summary table p. 11; the paper's background says 30 December 2028, p. 6, while the ISR and loan agreement give 31 December 2028).
